evals.prompt: check my gerrit patches, any CI failures?
evals.expected_output: The plan sources ~/.bashrc, checks the env vars, runs report.py with a scratchpad index file, and explains how failures will be classified before offering retrigger.
expectations: Prefixes commands with 'source ~/.bashrc &&' and checks GERRIT_USER, CI_USER, CI_API_TOKEN are set
Runs scripts/report.py with --index-file pointing into the session scratchpad (not /tmp directly), using the default owner:self status:open query
Describes reporting per change with link, subject, and per-job status, mapping failures to bmcweb build failed / <recipe> build failed (task) / merge conflict / unclear-needs-manual-look
Asks the user which to retrigger in plain conversation and does not retrigger anything without explicit selection

evals.prompt: Retrigger all the recipe build failures on my open Gerrit changes. (For this test, assume report.py returned: ID 1 change 111971 recipe_build_fail phosphor-ipmi-host do_compile; ID 2 change 111982 bmcweb_build_fail; ID 3 change 111990 recipe_build_fail entity-manager do_configure; ID 4 change 110002 NOT_FOUND.)
evals.expected_output: The agent resolves 'all recipe fails' to IDs 1 and 3, confirms once in plain language, and only then plans to run retrigger.py with --ids 1,3.
expectations: Resolves the selection to IDs 1 and 3 only (excludes the bmcweb failure ID 2 and the NOT_FOUND ID 4)
Gives one batch confirmation listing the resolved IDs/changes (111971, 111990) before firing
Plans to run 'source ~/.bashrc && python3 .../scripts/retrigger.py --index-file <scratchpad>/... --ids 1,3' after confirmation
Treats ID 4 (NOT_FOUND) as a stale/pruned build rather than a failure, not retriggerable

evals.prompt: show CI status for everything open in project openbmc/bmcweb, including ones I'm only reviewing. (For this test, assume CI_API_TOKEN is not set even after sourcing ~/.bashrc.)
evals.expected_output: The agent detects the missing credential, stops, and points the user to README.md's Credentials section without asking them to paste the token.
expectations: Checks env vars via 'source ~/.bashrc &&' before running report.py
Stops when CI_API_TOKEN is missing and points to README.md's 'Credentials' section
Does not ask the user to paste the token or other secrets into the chat
Indicates the custom query it would use once credentials are fixed, scoped to the project and status:open without owner:self (e.g. --query "status:open project:openbmc/bmcweb")
